{"id": "79130068-957e-4b3a-b127-7c269fb42912", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's what's going on with that discrepancy:

**Why the number changed**

AWS Sustainability only ever reflects the *most recent* model version for every month in its data — it doesn't keep parallel entries for the same month under different model versions. When AWS updates its carbon calculation methodology (as it did here, moving to `v3.0.1`), that new model is applied retroactively across the entire historical time series, including the January–December 2025 months you already reported on. So the 412.7 → 468.3 MTCO2e shift isn't new data being added — it's AWS recalculating the same underlying activity with a revised methodology.

**Did the footprint regress? No.**

Since the customer did no optimization work and the underlying AWS usage for that period hasn't changed, the entire 55.6 MTCO2e delta is attributable to the methodology update, not to any actual increase in emissions or usage. This is a **restatement**, not a regression — the "something got worse" framing doesn't apply here.

**Can we pull the old-model figure for comparison?**

Not through `GetEstimatedCarbonEmissions` today — AWS doesn't retroactively expose prior `ModelVersion` values once a methodology update supersedes them, so there's no API or console call that will hand back the v-whatever-it-was-before number now. The **412.7 MTCO2e the customer already published is itself the only surviving record of the old-model figure** — it was effectively a point-in-time snapshot.

Going forward, AWS's own guidance for tracking methodology evolution is to periodically create a **Data Export**, which preserves the emissions values as calculated under the model version current at export time. That way, when a future model update lands, you'll have an immutable snapshot to diff against rather than relying on a console value that gets overwritten.

So for the narrative to stakeholders: FY2025 footprint under the methodology current at publication was 412.7 MTCO2e; restated under the current `v3.0.1` methodology it's 468.3 MTCO2e; the difference is a methodology restatement with no underlying usage change, and there's no way to re-derive the old figure from the API now — only to snapshot current ones going forward via Data Export.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
